problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=1,$ $x=3,$ $y=0,$ $y=2,$ $z=-1,$ $z=1.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=(y-{x}^{2})\,i+xy\,j+3xz\,k,$ find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-{x}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(3xz) \\  & =(-2x)+x+3x \\  & =2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}2x\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}2x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}2x\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z \\  & =[{x}^{2}]_{x=1}^{x=3}\cdot (2-0)\cdot (1-(-1)) \\  & =(9-1)\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =32.\end{aligned}
$$
